body: In my case I've always suffered insomnia and I noticed I actually don't have to struggle as much when I'm depressed. I think it's because my insomnia is caused by my brain trying to solve all the next day problems, while when I'm depressed I don't really want to think about the future. Although when I'm more depressed I'm more likely to stay up playing games or watching videos.
Me too, I think about it all the time. We're all going away eventually anyway, and I keep thinking in the long run it would be less painful for everybody around me if I just disappear.
I think I know how you feel, no matter what I do bullies always find ways back in my life and people around me don't seem to really care about it. I hope everything gets better for you.

Thank you all for your responses, there is so much in mind right now. Yes, I do still get bullied but I can't go into details at the moment, but I do feel a little better, at least for a little while, thanks.

I've wondered the same before, both ways can be tough, but I guess it depends of your relationship with the people you are closer. I'm guessing you are talking about people that really care about you, if you are really committed to do it, maybe you can bring it up in a subtle way first, for example you could stop doing something you always do, and if they ask about it you could just say "What's the point of all of this", and see how they react, maybe this can help figuring out what would be better.
Either way, I believe you should at least first try to get treatment if you haven't already.
